Apple Pie - AEG BE3002420M

Classic double-crust apple pie adapted to the confirmed AEG Competence BE3002420M manual: Conventional Cooking, shelf position 1, 180 C, 70-90 min. The Kenwood KWL90.244SI handles the shortcrust dough, and the Adam apple slicer speeds up coring before final thin slicing.

8 generous slices2 hr 35 minMedium

1AssumptionsWhat I decided for you — override anything here

  • One 20-22 cm pie dish or similar oven-safe dish is used.
  • One cook is assumed.
  • Firm tart-sweet apples are used; reduce filling sugar if the apples are very sweet.
  • The AEG oven has no numbered programs for this recipe; use the named dial function Conventional Cooking.
  • The manual text confirms voltage and functions, but not total wattage or a printed full oven temperature range.

2Required

hands-on 0:50unattended 1:352 hr 35 min

Timeline

Checkpoints — all true before moving on

Ingredients

  • plain wheat flour350 gplus extra for rolling
  • cold unsalted butter225 g1-2 cm cubes
  • white sugar35 gfor dough
  • fine salt4 gabout 3/4 tsp
  • egg1for dough
  • sour cream or cold water60-90 gadd only enough to bind
  • apples1.1 kgbefore peeling/coring
  • brown sugar80-110 gto taste
  • lemon juice20 mlbalances sweetness
  • ground cinnamon6 gabout 2 tsp
  • potato starch or corn starch25 gbinds juices
  • breadcrumbs or semolina20 goptional, under filling
  • egg1beaten for egg wash
  • coarse sugar15 goptional topping

3Steps

  1. 1

    Prepare cold dough ingredientsCook

    WorktopKnife, scale, bowlKeep butter cold8 min

    Flour, cold butter, dough sugar, salt, egg, sour cream or cold water

    Cube the butter. Weigh flour, sugar, and salt. Keep butter cold until it goes into the mixer.

    Butter is cold and cubed; dry ingredients are weighed.

  2. 2

    Mix shortcrust doughCook

    Kenwood Titanium Chef Patissier XL KWL90.244SI5 L stainless bowl or 7 L EasyWarm bowl; stainless K-beaterLow speed until sandyspeed 1-2 only until clumps form10-12 min

    Dry ingredients, cold butter, egg, sour cream or cold water

    Mix flour, sugar, and salt. Add butter and mix until pea-sized. Add egg, then sour cream or cold water a spoonful at a time. Stop as soon as the dough clumps.

    Dough holds together when squeezed but is not smooth or warm.

  3. 3

    Divide and chillCook

    RefrigeratorCovered dough portionsCold storage30 min minimum

    Dough, wrap or covered container

    Divide dough into one larger base piece and one smaller top piece. Flatten into disks, cover, and chill.

    Dough is firm enough to roll without smearing butter.

  4. 4

    Prepare apple fillingCook

    WorktopAdam apple slicer, knife, large bowlManual slicer: 12 wedges, then knife-slice to 3-5 mm20 min

    Apples, sugar, lemon juice, cinnamon, starch

    Peel apples if desired. Core with the apple slicer, then cut wedges into thin slices. Toss with brown sugar, lemon juice, cinnamon, and starch.

    Apple slices are evenly coated and just starting to release juice.

  5. 5

    Preheat AEG ovenCook

    AEG Competence BE3002420MWire shelf on shelf position 1Conventional Cooking, 180 C15 min preheat

    AEG oven, wire shelf

    Set the function dial to Conventional Cooking, the symbol with two horizontal bars. Set 180 C. Put the wire shelf on shelf position 1.

    Oven is fully preheated before the pie goes in.

  6. 6

    Assemble pieCook

    WorktopPie dish, rolling pin, pastry brushRoll base slightly larger than dishcut vents in top15-20 min

    Chilled dough, apple filling, breadcrumbs/semolina, egg wash

    Roll the base and fit it into the dish. Sprinkle breadcrumbs or semolina if using. Add apples. Roll the top, cover, seal edges, cut vents, brush with beaten egg, and add coarse sugar if using.

    Top is sealed and vented; no large tears in the crust.

  7. 7

    BakeCook

    AEG Competence BE3002420MWire shelf, shelf position 1Conventional Cooking, 180 C70-90 min

    Assembled pie

    Bake on shelf position 1. Check at 70 min. If the rim browns too early, shield the edge loosely with foil while the centre finishes.

    Crust is deep golden and apple juices bubble through the vents.

  8. 8

    Cool and sliceCook

    CounterKnife, pie serverRoom temperature30 min minimum60 min cleaner slices

    Baked pie, cooling rack or heatproof counter

    Cool before cutting so the starch can set the apple juices.

    Slices lift without the filling flooding out.

  • Wash hands, tools, and work surface after handling raw egg.
  • Cool leftovers, then refrigerate if keeping longer than the day of baking.
  • Reheat slices until hot throughout if serving later.
